source_title: Man Utd news: How do Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher view Michael Carrick's situation? - BBC
source_excerpt:
Gary Neville says managers sometimes need to be sacked "for their own good" as he reflected on Manchester United's decision to persist with under-pressure Michael Carrick.
The club are 16th in the Premier League, just one point above the relegation zone, following a dismal 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth on Sunday.
Carrick was widely expected to be sacked after that loss, but the club have opted to give the 45-year-old head coach the opportunity to turn things around .
"I reckon what's happened in the 24 hours after Bournemouth is they have literally debated it back and forth," former Manchester United captain Neville said on the Stick To Football podcast.
"I don't know this, but I reckon they have debated it to the point where they have got themselves into a muddle and thought: 'We'll just stay with him.'
"I think staying with him is a result of lack of planning, lack of available options and lack of decision-making around the two people that probably are available - that's when you're really struggling.
"Sometimes a manager needs sacking for their own good. I needed sacking at Valencia . I was happy they put me out of my misery."
It is understood that the club's hierarchy has explored the possibility of replacing Carrick, with former Newcastle United boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany and Bayern Munich head coach Julian Nagelsmann under consideration.
Former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said: "He can never say it publicly but I think Michael Carrick would want to be put out of his misery, I really do.
"The thought of going into that training ground now and trying to do that team talk before Chelsea , when you know the players just aren't having it at all.
"Those players know Carrick isn't going to be there in two or three weeks. He knows it, they know it, everybody knows it."
